preconditions: Authenticated endpoints a, b, c, d have inc exposed.
a and b subscribe to napplet:profile/open; c subscribes to napplet:profile/opened; d subscribes to napplet:profile/open-other.
Topic ACL allows the exact tested topic.

assertions: b receives inc.event with unchanged topic and payload.
a receives no echo of its emission.
c and d receive no delivery from this emission.
The delivered sender is the runtime-attested identifier for a.

preconditions: Authenticated endpoint a emits; b subscribes to the exact topic; ACL permits it.

assertions: The runtime ignores or rejects the supplied sender.
If the emission is delivered, its sender is the attested endpoint-a identity, never endpoint-victim.

preconditions: a and b are live authenticated endpoints with inc.
Runtime channel ACL denies a opening a channel to b.

assertions: The result carries id open-1 and an error.
No channel is created; b receives no successful channel-open notification.

preconditions: a and b are live authenticated endpoints with inc.
Channel ACL allows the open.

assertions: The target inc.channel.opened is enqueued before the successful opener result is sent.
The result echoes open-2; both endpoints receive the same channel identifier and runtime-attested peer identity.
This ordering is enqueue/send ordering, not a requirement that a target application callback runs first.

preconditions: A channel opens while the target has no onOpened handler.
One incoming message arrives before a ChannelHandle.on handler exists.
Configured buffers have capacity for this scenario.

assertions: The retained ChannelHandle reaches the late onOpened handler.
Handle creation precedes the delivered channel message.
The retained message reaches the late message handler instead of being silently dropped.

preconditions: A ChannelHandle exists and becomes terminal before onClosed is registered.

assertions: The late handler receives the retained terminal ChannelClosed record.

preconditions: A finite incoming message buffer is configured and its limit is recorded.
No message handler drains the buffer.

steps: Send enough channel messages to exceed the configured buffer.

assertions: Overflow closes the channel and notifies both endpoints.
The binding does not silently discard messages while leaving the channel apparently active.

preconditions: a has an open channel to authenticated endpoint b.

steps: Load a replacement endpoint from the same manifest.

assertions: The surviving a receives channel closure with reason peer destroyed.
The replacement receives a new endpoint identifier; the previous identifier is not reused during the runtime session.
The old channel does not transfer to the replacement; another open is required.

preconditions: theme is exposed; shell is absent.
An active minimal theme exists and policy permits the query.

assertions: theme.get.result returns the configured theme with id without-shell.
No shell readiness exchange is required.

preconditions: shell and theme are exposed to an authenticated endpoint.
The harness delays environment delivery while permitting the theme query.

steps: Call theme.get before shell.init is delivered.

assertions: The theme operation is serviced independently of shell readiness.
Delaying shell.init does not serve as authorization for any other domain.

preconditions: An authenticated endpoint has shell exposed.

assertions: Exactly one shell.init is produced for the first readiness signal.
The duplicate creates no new session, identity, policy, or environment delivery.

preconditions: Endpoint a has shell and theme exposed.
Endpoint b has shell and identity exposed.

assertions: a receives an environment describing only its exposed domains and services.
b-only grants are not disclosed or granted to a by that snapshot.

preconditions: shell and theme are injected; identity is absent.
shell.init has not arrived.

assertions: supports(theme) returns true locally.
supports(identity) returns false locally.
Neither call waits for shell.init or emits a wire availability query.

preconditions: identity is exposed; no user/signer is connected.

assertions: identity.getPublicKey.result carries id identity-1 and pubkey as the empty string.
The response is successful without an error field.

preconditions: An authenticated loaded napplet has identity exposed.
A user/signer was connected and is now disconnected.

assertions: identity.changed reports pubkey as the empty string.
The verified napplet endpoint identity is not renegotiated as a result of the user change.

preconditions: theme is exposed; an active theme has only background/text/primary colors.
Query policy permits access.

assertions: The result echoes theme-1 and contains all three required colors.
Omitted fonts, background media, and title do not make the theme invalid.

preconditions: a has theme exposed without an R or O theme advertisement.
b advertises theme but runtime policy does not expose it.

assertions: a receives theme.changed automatically, with no wire subscription.
b receives no theme.changed.
Manifest advertisements do not substitute for domain exposure.

preconditions: A binding has an onChanged handler registered for exposed theme.

steps: Deliver another theme.changed through the binding.

assertions: The closed handler is not invoked.
No theme subscribe or unsubscribe wire message is introduced.

preconditions: Source has intent exposed and a verified catalog identity.
A compatible installed target advertises the exact convention and role.
Runtime policy allows delivery; the selected lifecycle closes the source before target startup.
The target subsequently becomes ready; terminal failure is not injected.

assertions: The runtime sends one successful intent.invoke.result with id intent-1 before closing the source.
Acceptance represents delivery responsibility, not target processing.
The delivery is retained independently of the source and delivered after the target is ready.
A later target failure, if separately tested, is not a second result to the source.

preconditions: Source and eligible target have verified catalog entries and authenticated endpoints.
An unrelated third napplet is loaded.
Normal installed-handler selection resolves the eligible target and policy permits delivery.

assertions: Only the resolved target receives the intent delivery and payload.
Delivery sender is the runtime-attested catalog identity of the source.
The unrelated napplet receives neither payload nor sender metadata from this invocation.

preconditions: A verified target advertises profile and napplet:profile/open.
The manifest requires a domain the configured runtime cannot expose to that target.

steps: Attempt invocation of the advertised convention.

assertions: The runtime applies the complete required-capability compatibility and policy checks before acceptance.
Role and intent advertisements do not widen exposed domains or authorize execution.
